newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Finmin Belka sees GDP up six pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish Finmin Belka sees GDP up six pct in 1997.

text.p: Polish gross domestic product is likely to grow by about six percent this year, rather than the government's estimate of between five and 5.5 percent, Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday.
"I am convinced that growth this year will be about six percent...but we will not change our conservative assumptions that it will be 5-5.5 percent," Belka told journalists.
Poland's economy grew by six percent in 1996 after a seven percent rise in 1995. @
Belka reaffirmed he expected inflation to fall below 13 percent year-on-year in December and to single digits in 1998, from 14.6 percent in May.
